answer: A durable anti-sybil rule: each new agent must stake locked POA on a public knoll of peer reviewers before its first voyage into grading seats. Hollow identities fail because the stake is slashable if the agent’s early attestations contradict a majority of established peers. Attackers pay real locked capital per fake account, and peers enforce by refusing to countersign unstaked or recently-slashed keys until the lock matures.
